alt: A scaled bar from 632 to 661 divided into the rules of Abu Bakr (632–634), Umar (634–644), Uthman (644–656) and Ali (656–661), with key events for each: Usama's army, the Ridda wars and the collection of the Qur'an; Umar's conquests and administration; Uthman's expansion, navy, standard copies and the siege; and Ali's battles of the Camel, Siffin and Nahrawan.
caption: Four rules in under thirty years; Umar and Uthman ruled longest.

after: ## Abu Bakr (632–634): holding the community together
alt: Five problems and Abu Bakr's responses: choosing a leader at the Saqifa; sending Usama's army despite danger at home; the Ridda wars against tribes refusing zakat and false prophets, ending at Yamama; collecting the Qur'an after huffaz died; and nominating Umar after consultation.
caption: Abu Bakr met each crisis firmly and kept the community and the Qur'an intact.

alt: Umar at the centre with four areas: expansion through Yarmuk, Qadisiyya, Jerusalem, Egypt and Nahawand; administration with governors, separate qadis, the bayt al-mal, the diwan, garrison towns and the Hijri calendar; accountability through checks on governors; and religion, gathering Muslims for tarawih.
caption: Conquest, institutions and accountability: Umar turned a community into a state.

alt: Two columns. Achievements: chosen by the council of six, expansion into North Africa, Armenia and Persia, the first navy and Cyprus, standard copies of the Qur'an and the enlarged Prophet's Mosque. Difficulties: relatives appointed as governors, complaints from Egypt, Kufa and Basra, the siege of his house and his killing in 656.
caption: Uthman's rule brought growth and the standard Qur'an, but also division.

alt: Six steps through Ali's rule: chosen in Madinah in 656; the Battle of the Camel over punishing Uthman's killers; the capital moved to Kufa; arbitration at Siffin in 657; the defeat of the Kharijites at Nahrawan in 658; and his death at Kufa in 661.
caption: Camel, Siffin, Nahrawan: three crises in three years, in that order.

alt: Four cards: Abu Bakr chosen by discussion at the Saqifa and a public pledge; Umar nominated by Abu Bakr after consultation; Uthman chosen by a council of six through Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf; and Ali chosen in Madinah after Uthman's death. The members of the council of six are listed.
caption: Four different methods, each resting on consultation and consent.

alt: A vertical chain: a large empire with new Muslims; disputes over recitation resolved by standardisation; criticism of relatives as governors; complaints from Egypt, Kufa and Basra; an alleged letter turning the Egyptian delegation back; the siege of his house, where he refused to let others fight for him; and his killing in 656.
caption: Each difficulty led to the next; include Uthman's response at every step.
